whatsnew: **Alerts fire on the first occurrence.** Thirty-five shipped alerts compared their result against a threshold of 1 under a strict greater-than test: a yes-or-no check could never fire, and a count needed two events before it spoke. They now fire at the first occurrence. Existing installs receive the corrected definitions on upgrade, and an alert you have tuned is left exactly as you left it.

**Space and I/O alerts read the right numbers.** Five alerts, including the Critical database-space and log-space alerts, measured only master; they now check every database on the server. The I/O error alert counts unrepaired suspect pages rather than a lifetime stall figure that fired without end on a healthy server. Read and write latency alerts measure a five-second window, not a since-startup average that could never clear.

**Audit scores count only checks that can run.** In the Diagnostics Roadmap a check no deployed script can emit used to score as a pass on every server. The Roadmap now leaves it out of the score, under the same rule the sp_Blitz Dashboard already applied. An audit file that cannot be read is named on both pages with its numbers cleared, where it used to score as if every check had passed.

**The Servers page reports what it checked this session.** After a restart every connection shows as not checked, with the date it last connected, in place of a green status nobody measured. A connection with no server names says nothing was contacted. When some servers answer and one fails, the ones that answered are recorded, not a total failure.

**Assessments name only the servers they measured.** The Vulnerability Assessment cover lists the servers that answered, with a note naming the ones that did not. A run with zero results no longer reads as compliant, and the progress toast says when a server was not measured. Server Comparison shows "Not measured" for a server it did not score rather than painting it red, and the dbatools runner shows what a command wrote to standard error where it used to say "No results returned".

**Reports say "Not measured" where nothing was measured.** In the Audit Evidence PDF an audit log that could not be read prints "Not measured" in place of "Total Audit Events: 0", and the report states the scope of the findings it hashed; the fixed "Last 30 days" line is gone. In the Risk Register PDF a check that could not run is labelled "Could not run" with no server-impact count beside it.

**Four security holes closed.** Text rendered from markdown on the DBA Dashboard, Governance, Playbooks and QuickCheck pages can no longer run a script or open a javascript: link, and a dashboard panel whose SQL would run an operating-system command is refused before it is cached. A request whose Host header is not a name this server answers to is refused with a 400 before any page loads, which shuts DNS-rebinding out of the loopback interface; the accepted names are written to the log at startup, and the 400 itself names the setting that adds a name. A damaged access-control store now holds a local anonymous session at viewer, with a banner on every page, where it used to grant admin quietly.

**Local recovery can require a password.** Onboarding asks for a recovery password once the first admin exists; declining is remembered. Settings > Security & Access holds the control and warns while none is set. With a password set, local recovery opens the recovery form only, never an admin session.

**Disk I/O names the instance it sampled.** The source pill shows the instance that was actually measured, and a connection profile that lists several instances says it was sampled at its first instance only.
